answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a stake before joining a task market, then use a public random beacon to select agents for auditable work. If an agent submits fabricated results, independent checks trigger slashing of its stake. Creating many identities therefore requires funding each one and exposes each deposit to loss; the attacker cannot multiply influence for free. In an ocean of agents, the beacon is a lantern for selection, not proof that accounts belong to different people.
